capability_review.scope: post-finalization diagnosis; no model or tool decision
capability_review.overall_assessment: This finalized forecast run beat its baseline decisively (validation 0.124 vs 0.779) and progressed cleanly through the full feature toolbox: date decomposition, frequency encoding, target encoding, rolling-history aggregates, filtering, and grouped statistics, finishing at 42 features. No tool refusal occurred, so every attempted operation was expressible. Each feature stage produced a measurable improvement down to a plateau (~0.124–0.132), and the GBM/loss-family models cluster tightly around that plateau, with the shipped blend (0.1242) essentially matching the best single model (0.1245). There is no evidence of a generic capability, tooling, model-selection, or data-contract shortage blocking a better result; the remaining error appears data-natured rather than tool-limited. The one genuine caution is measurement/serving hygiene: target- and rolling-history features fitted in-sample can inflate the time-collated validation (0.124) relative to the held-out period (0.132), and the declared serving contract lists no required input streams. Per the review rules, the internal test score is retrospective reference only and supports no choice, refit, or shipment.

findings.title: No generic tool or procedure gap demonstrated; feature pipeline and model families were sufficient
findings.generic_capability: Joint, iteratively-measured feature engineering spanning date decomposition, frequency encoding, target encoding, rolling history, row filtering, and grouped statistics, followed by an ensemble of several loss families
findings.why_existing_tools_insufficient: Existing tools were sufficient; no insufficiency was demonstrated. Feature stages were individually measured and refined scoring from ~0.225 down to ~0.124, all transforms fit without refusal (refusals=0), and the distinct model families that could be expressed all converged to the same plateau. Nothing in the evidence shows a useful operation that the available tools could not express.
findings.alternative_explanation: The residual error after ~0.124 may be irreducible noise, or could stem from un-tuned per-family hyperparameters and a near-uniform blend weighting (the shipped blend barely exceeds the best single model). None of these are established by a score gap alone, so they do not qualify as a proven model-selection deficiency.
findings.leakage_or_serving_risk: Target-encoded and rolling-history features fitted in-sample can be optimistic when the validation fold is time-adjacent to training; consistently, the held-out scores (≈0.128–0.136) exceed the time-validation (0.1242), and a large CV-vs-validation spread (≈0.24 vs ≈0.12) signals that temporal dependencies dominate. The declared serving contract lists no required input streams, so reproducibility of these target-derived features at serving must be verified. The internal test score is retrospective only and must not drive model choice or shipment.
findings.testable_hypothesis: Re-running the identical feature steps on an extended look-back without any target-derived input inside the validation window, and scoring on a fresh, later time-collated holdout, should reproduce a validation score within the observed ~0.12–0.14 band; if it does not, target/rolling encodings were leaking across the split.
